q: Gromov's non-squeezing theorem (1985) states that a symplectic map cannot embed a ball B(r) into a cylinder Z(R) = {z : |z₁|² + |z₂|² < R²} × ℝ^{2n-2} if:
exp: Non-squeezing: a symplectic embedding of B(r) into Z(R) requires r ≤ R. Despite the cylinder having infinite volume, symplectic rigidity prevents compressing in the symplectic directions. This shows symplectic maps are far more rigid than volume-preserving maps.
